events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.96)
events.body:
The cancellation was made by the rider (F2), so the fee can only stand through NS-0's rider-cancellation branch, which for an immediate booking is NS-4 [F2][NS-0]. The rider cancelled at 14:07:55, 2 min 55 s (175 s) after the 14:05:00 acceptance — inside the 3-minute free window — so nothing is chargeable and the $6.61 on record must be returned in full [F2][F5][NS-4].

Independently, the no-show basis fails. There is no arrival confirmation at all: the platform recorded no driver tap on "I'm Here" and no automatic arrival (driver_pressed_here_at and driver_arrived_at both null), so NS-1(i) is unsatisfied on either branch [F3][F4][NS-1]. The GPS record puts the driver 2,189 m from the pickup point at the moment of cancellation and never within 200 m, so NS-1(ii) also fails [F1][NS-1].

The driver's statement "I was on my way when the rider cancelled" is not a passenger no-show claim [F10][NS-3], and his chat message at 14:06 said he was "5 min more" — he was still inbound, not waiting at the pickup point [F8][NS-1]. Since the fee could only be retained on a no-show basis the driver never asserts, no part of it is his [F10][NS-3].

The disputed item is the cancellation fee alone, $6.61, with a 1.0× surge and no other add-on on the fare record, so the amount to be returned is exactly $6.61 [F5][F6][NS-4]. Under NS-7 that refund is issued as a Ryde voucher rather than cash [F5][NS-7]. The traffic band and weather facts (free-flowing, no incidents, fair) only show the driver's "traffic is slow" remark is uncorroborated; they are not needed for the outcome and change neither the amount nor any account action [F11][F12][F13][NS-4].

No flag_account arises: RD-6 is not triggered (no route-deviation case and no refund computed under RD-2), and NS-2's flag attaches only where the driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS placed him outside the pickup radius — he did not tap it at all [F3][F4][NS-2]. The driver's clean profile (4.0 y, 4.77, 0 upheld) is a profile fact and is not used to decide the case, and the rider's profile likewise [F14][F15][NS-4].

Safety screen: I read both chat messages ("How long will you be?"; "5 min more, traffic is slow"), the driver's post-trip statement and the complaint. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — the dispute is purely about the fee [F7][F8][F10][SAFE-1].

Evidence: the record settles every element the ruling needs — the cancellation party and time (F2), the missing arrival confirmation (F3, F4), the driver's distance (F1), the fee (F5) and a complete, fully timestamped chat (F9) — so no gap requires escalation.

The two advocates now agree on every material point, including both revised asks for refund_full of $6.61 [C1][C5][D1][D4][D8], and the trace's settled elements (cancelled_by = rider; cancellation at 175 s) fix the NS-4 outcome.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (non-cash) under NS-7; no account action against either party.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled at 14:07:55, only 2 minutes 55 seconds after the 14:05:00 acceptance, i.e. within the 3-minute window, so no cancellation fee is chargeable.
The driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform recorded no automatic arrival (driver_pressed_here_at is null; driver_arrived_at is null), so NS-1(i) is not satisfied on either branch.
At the moment of cancellation the driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 2189 m — well beyond the 200 m arrival radius — and he never came within 200 m at any time, so NS-1(ii) fails.

The chat record shows the rider asking "How long will you be?" and the driver answering "5 min more, traffic is slow" at 14:06, which corroborates the driver was still minutes away rather than waiting at the pickup point.
Because NS-1 (i), (ii) and (iii) all fail, the $6.61 cancellation fee charged on record must be refunded in full to the rider.

The driver's own explanation was merely "I was on my way when the rider cancelled", which is not a passenger no-show claim and concedes he had not reached the pickup point; a driver who cancels or is not at the pickup point without a valid reason leaves the rider with no fee.

Traffic on the route was free-flowing (Stevens Road band 4, 30–39 km/h) with no incidents and fair weather, so the driver's "traffic is slow" explanation is not borne out and does not excuse his absence from the pickup point.
The rider's profile shows no upheld no-show or route disputes in the last 90 days (0 upheld), so nothing in the rider's history supports treating the cancellation as abusive.

weaknesses: The complaint asserts the driver "was nowhere near", which is correct on the GPS record (F1: 2189 m), but the rider cancelled seconds before the 3-minute mark (F2: 2 min 55 s) after having asked the driver how long he would be (F7) — the other side may argue the rider knew the driver was still inbound and cancelled opportunistically just inside the free window.

The driver has a strong record (F15: 4.0 years, 4.77 rating, 652 trips, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) and may argue at 14:07:55 he was close; the GPS fact F1 contradicts that, but a judge may give weight to the near-miss timing in F2 and decline any account flag.
Chat is only two messages (F9); there is no message from the rider stating a reason for cancelling, so the rider's motive must be inferred from F1/F2 alone.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 2 min 55 s after matching, so the $6.61 cancellation fee was not earned and must be refunded in full under the rider-cancellation rule for immediate bookings.
The fare record shows the only charge in dispute is the $6.61 cancellation fee, with no surge and no other add-on, so the amount to be refunded is exactly $6.61 and is computable from the fare fact.
The record shows no arrival confirmation at all: the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform recorded no automatic arrival, so no no-show basis for retaining the fee exists.

The driver was 2,189 m from the pickup point when the rider cancelled and never came within 200 m; the driver does not claim the rider was a no-show, and a fee resting on an unfulfilled arrival requirement must be returned to the rider.

The driver told the rider at 14:06 that he was "5 min more" and the rider cancelled at 14:07:55, before that stated time elapsed; this is consistent with an ordinary rider cancellation rather than any abuse of the waiting or cancellation button.
The chat record is complete with both messages timestamped, so the cancellation timing and the driver's en-route message can be read on the record without any evidentiary gap requiring escalation.

The driver's record (4.0 years, 4.77 rating, 652 trips, zero disputes and zero upheld in 90 days) supports treating this as a one-off service shortfall rather than an abuse case; no flag_account action is warranted against him.
Refund of the $6.61 as a Ryde voucher is the correct form of relief, the dispute having been raised promptly after the trip rather than as a cash claim.

weaknesses: The driver never reached the pickup point (F1, F3, F4) and said only that he "was on my way" (F10), so there is no basis on this record to retain any part of the $6.61 or to counter-charge the rider.
The driver's own message "5 min more, traffic is slow" (F8) shows he was still several minutes out at 14:06, which the rider will cite as her reason for cancelling.
Retaining a fee for a 2:55 cancellation would invite an abuse-of-fee finding against the driver's otherwise clean record (F15), so conceding the refund is the safer course for the account.

points.response: Agreed and adopted: the cancellation at 14:07:55, 2 min 55 s after the 14:05:00 acceptance (F2), falls inside the 3-minute window, so NS-4 grants no fee and the $6.61 on record (F5) must be returned.
Agreed: the only disputed charge is the $6.61 cancellation fee with a 1.0x surge and no other add-on (F5, F6), so the refund is exactly $6.61 payable as a Ryde voucher under NS-7.
Agreed: driver_pressed_here_at and driver_arrived_at are both null (F3, F4), so NS-1(i) is unsatisfied and NS-2 requires full refund of the fee.

Agreed: 2189 m closest approach and never within 200 m (F1) defeats NS-1(ii), and since the driver does not assert a no-show, the rider keeps no liability; no flag_account is sought against the driver, whose record is clean (F15).

Agreed that the driver's own "5 min more, traffic is slow" at 14:06 (F8) fixes his position as still inbound at the 14:07:55 cancellation (F2); I add that the traffic record shows free-flowing conditions on the route (F11, F12) and fair weather (F13), so the slowdown was not route-wide.
Agreed: both chat messages are timestamped and the record is complete (F9), so no gap under G12 arises and the timing can be read directly from F2.
Agreed; the rider seeks no account flag against the driver — the rider's own history also shows zero upheld disputes in 90 days (F14) — so the remedy is confined to the fee.
Agreed: the $6.61 refund (F5) is properly issued as a non-cash Ryde voucher under NS-7, the rider having raised the dispute promptly after the trip.
We agree: the driver's client has no answer on this point, and the record shows the 2 min 55 s cancellation at 14:07:55 (F2), inside the 3-minute free window, so nothing is chargeable under NS-4.

Agreed, but the finding should be stated precisely: the platform recorded no arrival by tap or automatically (F3, F4), so the NS-1(i) arrival confirmation is absent on both branches and no no-show fee can stand.

Conceded; GPS puts the driver 2,189 m away at the moment of cancellation and never within 200 m (F1), so NS-1(ii) fails and the fee must be returned in the amount of $6.61 as shown on the fare record (F5).

Accepted: the two timestamped messages show the rider asking "How long will you be?" and the driver replying "5 min more, traffic is slow" (F7, F8, F9), which corroborates that the driver was still en route, not waiting at the pickup point.

Agreed on the relief and the amount: NS-1 fails on (i) and (ii), so under NS-2 the $6.61 shown as charged in F5 is refunded in full, in voucher form per NS-7 — which is exactly the outcome this side already requested.

Accepted that F10 is not a no-show claim — the driver only says he was on his way — and the rider is therefore not liable; the record nevertheless shows the rider cancelled, not the driver (F2), so no cancellation-rate consequence against the driver arises.

Conceded: traffic was band 4, 30–39 km/h on Stevens Road with no incidents and fair weather (F11, F12, F13), so the driver's "traffic is slow" message (F8) is not corroborated and gives no exemption; this does not change the outcome, which already refunds the full $6.61 (F5).

Agreed the rider's 90-day history shows no upheld disputes (F14), and this side does not seek any account action against her; equally, the driver's own clean record of 4.0 years, 4.77 rating and zero upheld disputes (F15) is why no flag_account should attach to him either.
